premises.text: Building camera-connected software is slow and expensive because of local-network issues, fragmented camera SDKs, and laborious per-customer deployment
premises.evidence_span: local network issues. Cameras, like any local network device, will misbehave

premises.text: EverCam exposes a hosted developer web API that handles camera connectivity for end users, works with any internet-connected camera, and makes camera apps as easy to distribute as phone apps
premises.evidence_span: expose to the software developer a beautiful, modern, hosted web API

premises.text: EverCam monetizes with a recurring fee on a per-camera basis
premises.evidence_span: EverCam is generating a recurring fee on a per-camera basis

value.text: Software developers can build live-image applications on cameras without wrestling hardware/network complexity, improving customer services
value.evidence_span: make these cameras programmable, and thereby to unleash a whole new category of software development based around the live image

causal_links.evidence_span: This is very, very typical of many camera-related projects
We try and reduce all of that complexity
EverCam is generating a recurring fee on a per-camera basis

notes: Network, fragmentation, and per-customer install pains folded as one camera-dev problem (§4.1.6). Connectivity helper, any-camera guarantee, and app-store ease folded as API platform cascade (§4.1.7). Tunstall 12-month/$1M failure and one-month success treated as evidence, not premises. Android/iOS analogy coded as value framing. Anti-template: problem, API product, and recurring fee separately revisable.
